# colormath conventions

This app is a **colormath app**: the CI gates, their local `make` mirrors, and
the agent tooling all come from the shared infra repo
[ColorMath/ci](https://github.com/ColorMath/ci), pinned at an exact tag.
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` is a thin caller — the gate definitions live
upstream, not here. Consumer-side config lives in `.colormath/`: `audit.conf`
(the poetry groups that ship, plus the CVE allowlist), `ci.env` (non-secret
pytest env for CI) and, where a project needs extra install steps,
`ci-extra-install.sh`.

Three files in your repo are **vendored** and must never be hand-edited:
`Makefile.colormath`, `eslint.config.colormath.mjs`, and this file.

## The gates

Sixteen gates run in parallel on every PR. Each has a local `make` target that
mirrors CI exactly — same tool, same version, same config.

| Gate | Local mirror | How to pass |
|---|---|---|
| **ruff** (format + lint) | `make format-check` · `make lint` | Auto-fix first: `ruff format .` then `ruff check --fix .` (most repos wrap this as `make format` or `make fix`). |
| **tests** (JS + Python) | `make test` · `make lock-check` | Keep `pytest` and `vitest` green. `lock-check` is part of this gate: re-run `poetry lock` whenever you touch `pyproject.toml`. |
| **typecheck** (mypy) | `make typecheck` | Annotate new code. Strictness is per-directory in `[tool.mypy]`. |
| **docstrings** (interrogate) | `make docstrings` | Coverage ≥ the `fail-under` in `[tool.interrogate]`. |
| **migrations** (git) | `make migrations` | Fails when the base branch grew migrations your branch never saw — merging would leave multiple alembic heads. Fix by pulling the base branch, not by editing history. Run `git fetch origin` first so it reads the right base. |
| **import-linter** | `make import-linter` | Your `[tool.importlinter]` contracts hold — layer order, forbidden imports, independence. colormath ships the runner; the contracts are yours. |
| **jslint** (eslint) | `make jslint` | Hand-written JS passes lint. `eslint.config.js` is a thin caller of the vendored base. |
| **styles** (stylelint) | `make styles` | Design tokens only — no hardcoded `color`, `fill`, `stroke` or `font-size`. See **Code style** below. |
| **templates** (djlint) | `make templates` | Jinja templates well-formed per `[tool.djlint]`. |
| **sast** (bandit) | `make sast` | No Medium+ findings in app source. Don't introduce `shell=True`, unsafe yaml/pickle, hardcoded secrets. |
| **secrets** (gitleaks) | `make secrets` | Scans **full git history**, so a secret is not fixed by deleting it in a later commit. Keep secrets in gitignored files; allowlist genuinely public values in `.gitleaks.toml`. Needs gitleaks installed locally. |
| **a11y** (html-validate) | `make a11y` | Templates pass the `html-validate:a11y` preset — alt text, `label`/`for`, valid ARIA. |
| **deps** (pip-audit) | `make audit` | Locked, *shipped* deps have no actionable CVEs — dev tooling never trips it. Bump the dependency and re-lock; only if no in-range fix exists, allowlist it in `.colormath/audit.conf`. |
| **js-deps** (npm audit) | `make js-audit` | Shipped JS deps have no high+ CVEs (`--omit=dev`). |
| **dockerfile** (hadolint) | `make dockerfile` | Dockerfile best practices. Needs hadolint installed locally. |
| **diff-coverage** | `make coverage-diff` | **Lines you changed must be ≥90% covered.** Pre-existing untested code is never gated — only new and changed lines, so add tests for logic you add. |

A project may disable gates it hasn't burned down yet. Disabled gates are set
twice and the two **must stay in lockstep**: `enable-<gate>: false` in
`gates.yml`, and the matching target in `COLORMATH_PREFLIGHT_SKIP` in the
`Makefile`. Out of lockstep, preflight passes locally and CI fails — or worse,
preflight silently skips a gate CI still runs. This app's own list is in those
two files; treat them as the answer, not any prose description of them.

## Working rhythm

**Don't run the gate suite on every change.** It's slow and it kills iteration
speed. While building, run only the quick check tied to what you're editing —
the single test you're working on, and an auto-format after each change.

Then run the full local mirror **once**, as a pre-flight, right before opening
the PR:

```
make preflight   # every enabled gate, in order; mirrors CI exactly
```

If `make preflight` is green, the PR's gates will be too.

## Shipping

- **Ship branches with `/colormath:ship`** (from the colormath plugin). It is
  the one and only way to take a branch through the PR pipeline: it opens the
  PR, watches the gates, reads the review, triages the findings and stops at a
  merge recommendation. Do not hand-roll that loop with ad-hoc `gh` calls. If a
  request implies shipping — "open a PR", "get this reviewed", "push it up" —
  reach for `/colormath:ship` first.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, checks, reviews, comments).
- Every change ships through a pull request. Gates must be green before a
  review counts, and a review must be addressed before recommending merge.
- When you push a commit responding to review feedback, post a PR comment
  saying what you changed **and what you deliberately did not** — a silent push
  makes the reviewer re-derive your reasoning.
- You may push fixes to a feature branch. **Never push to the default branch,
  and never merge** — merging is always a human decision. Recommend, don't
  execute.

## Architecture conventions

- Request flow is `routes/` → `services/` → `models/`; external systems are
  wrapped in `adapters/`. Never import upward. Where the project writes
  `[tool.importlinter]` contracts, this is mechanically enforced rather than
  merely agreed.
- **Routes** parse input, resolve the caller, authorize, call a service, and
  render. **Services** own persistence. Keep ORM and SQL out of routes.
- Alembic needs the repo on the path: `PYTHONPATH=. poetry run alembic upgrade
  head` (`heads` / `history` likewise), or the project's `make migrate` wrapper.
- `alembic/versions/` is generated migration history — excluded from lint, and
  not a place to hand-edit past migrations. Fix a bad migration with a new one.

## Code style

- **Colors — single source of truth (hard rule).** Every color MUST resolve to
  a design token. **Never** write a hardcoded hex, `rgb(...)`, `hsl(...)` or CSS
  named color anywhere — not in templates, not in component CSS, not in inline
  `style=` attributes, not in SVGs used as UI. Need a shade that doesn't exist?
  Add a token and use it; do not inline the value. The `styles` gate enforces
  this for `color`, `fill`, `stroke` and `font-size`. *Where this app's tokens
  live, and what they're named, is in its own `AGENTS.md`.*
- Docstrings follow the Google convention (ruff `D` rules), with coverage held
  by the `docstrings` gate. Per-directory `D` ignores are debt: remove one when
  you bring a file up to standard, never add a new one.
- Structured logging: `logger.info("snake_case_event", key=value)`, not bare
  string messages.

## Architecture decision records

Significant architectural decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/adr/` — one
immutable file per decision.

- **Read before you change architecture.** Skim the index whenever you're about
  to alter a datastore or schema shape, a subsystem boundary, the auth or
  entitlement model, an external integration, or deployment topology. If an ADR
  covers it, the constraint is deliberate — don't "fix" it. Cite the ADR when
  your work follows or conflicts with it.
- **Ask the user first, then draft.** The decision is theirs to ratify; you
  write it up. Never record an architectural decision they haven't agreed to.
- **Write one when they make such a decision.** Next free number, kebab-case
  title, added to the index in the same commit and shipped in the PR that
  implements the decision. This includes deliberate *non*-decisions ("we are
  not doing X, because…").
- **Never rewrite an accepted ADR's decision.** Supersede it: write a new ADR
  and set the old one's status to `Superseded by ADR-NNNN` with a link.
- Not needed for ordinary implementation, bug fixes, shape-preserving
  refactors, or rules already written down. When it's arguable, it probably
  doesn't need one.
- Not CI-gated — `make preflight` doesn't check for ADRs. This is a convention.

## Guardrails

- **Never** hand-edit `Makefile.colormath`, `eslint.config.colormath.mjs`, or
  this file — all three are vendored from ColorMath/ci and a local edit is
  silently reverted by the next refresh.
- **Bumping colormath is a dedicated PR** that updates the `gates.yml` (and
  `review.yml`, where present) pins **and** runs
  `make colormath-update REF=vX.Y.Z`. The pins and the vendored files must stay
  in lockstep: miss the refresh and `make preflight` runs older gate scripts
  than CI, which is invisible until one of them changes.
- **Never** push to the default branch; merging is always a human decision.
- **Never** create, edit, or delete `.env` or other secret files. For a test
  fixture that needs an env file, use a throwaway name like `.env.citest`.
- Every CVE ignore added to `.colormath/audit.conf` needs a written
  justification and a revisit trigger. An allowlist entry with neither is
  indistinguishable from an unnoticed vulnerability.
